verified_signals.entity: Komercni banka / Moneta / Air Bank / UniCredit Bank CZ (shared deposit ATM network)
verified_signals.signal: UniCredit Bank joined the four-bank shared DEPOSIT ATM network on 16/02/2026, adding 144 deposit ATMs and taking the shared deposit pool to 'nearly a thousand' (temer tisic) deposit ATMs. The single-deposit cap was unified and raised from CZK 300,000 to CZK 350,000 across the whole shared network. Nearly 120 ATMs have been relocated since the start of 2026 from over-served city locations to under-served municipalities. January 2026 alone: more than 155,000 shared deposits worth nearly CZK 2bn; more than 1.8m shared deposits since the August-2024 deposit-sharing launch. KB clients can from February 2026 deposit using a digitalised payment card held in a phone or smartwatch (already live for Moneta and Air Bank).
verified_signals.source_name: Komercni banka press release (primary); UniCredit's 144-ATM contribution cross-checked in e15.cz and Penize.cz coverage of the same release
verified_signals.implies: Cash-recycling / deposit ATM hardware, cardless and NFC-wallet deposit software (deposit initiated by a tokenised card in a phone rather than a plastic card), shared-network transaction switching, routing and monitoring.
verified_signals.followup: Identify the supplier of the NFC/wallet deposit application layer and of the shared-network routing/switch; ask each of the four banks which of their deposit ATMs are recyclers versus deposit-only.
verified_signals.verifier_note: Opened the KB release directly. It states verbatim 'temer tisic vkladovych bankomatu', the CZK 300,000 -> 350,000 unified cap, 'temer 120 bankomatu' relocated since the start of the year, >155,000 January-2026 deposits worth nearly CZK 2bn, >1.8m deposits since August 2024, and the digitalised-card-in-phone-or-smartwatch capability from February 2026. The KB release itself does NOT print the '144' figure; I confirmed 144 UniCredit deposit ATMs from e15.cz and Penize.cz reporting on the same release, so that one number is press-sourced rather than primary. Note the shared network began as a WITHDRAWAL-sharing scheme in 2022 (KB + Moneta); deposit sharing started August 2024 - the researcher's Aug-2024 date is correct for deposits only.

Free of charge, requires a Moneta EUR account and a card linked to it, credited to the EUR account within minutes. The number of EUR-enabled machines is NOT disclosed.

verified_signals.implies: Multi-currency cash-acceptance recyclers, note-validation and denomination-recognition software for a second currency, and cash forecasting for a two-currency estate.

Only after those two steps will it consider further cutting manned cash desks. Moneta cut cash desks sharply during 2025: in August 2024 it had 134 branches all with a cash desk; at 01/01/2026 cash desks remained at only 41 of 123 branches, some open only part of the week.

verified_signals.entity: Czech banking sector - branch and cash-desk network (13 retail banks)
verified_signals.signal: [Census dated 01/01/2026, published 30/01/2026] The 13 Czech retail banks ran 1,426 branches of which only 548 still had a manned cash desk, versus 1,503 branches / 687 cash desks in August 2024 - 139 manned cash desks removed in ~17 months. Per bank at 01/01/2026 (branches, of which with cash desk): Ceska sporitelna 329 (115), Komercni banka 185 (103), Partners Banka 178 (0), CSOB 175 (64), Moneta 123 (41), Raiffeisenbank 116 (44), UniCredit 111 (43), Fio 86 (all), Creditas 33 (all), Air Bank 32 (0), mBank 29 (0), Oberbank 19 (17), Trinity 9 (2). Only Fio and Creditas still keep a manned desk at every branch. Coin machines: CSOB down from 15 branches to 9; KB has one and will not expand; UniCredit, Air Bank and Raiffeisenbank rule them out ('zcela zanedbatelna poptavka' - demand entirely negligible). UniCredit has moved 40%+ of branches to part-week cash desks and continues that model in 2026; Ceska sporitelna says it expects to close at least 'higher units' of branches during 2026.
verified_signals.source_name: Penize.cz survey of the banks (with named spokespeople for each bank)
verified_signals.implies: Every manned cash desk removed displaces cash into recyclers and assisted self-service. This is the core Printec recycler + cash-automation driver in Czechia, and it is sector-wide rather than one-bank.
verified_signals.followup: Map cash-desk closures to recycler deployment per bank; note the coin-machine (mincomat) market is effectively closed except at Moneta and CSOB - do not lead with coin handling elsewhere.
verified_signals.verifier_note: Retrieved via curl with a desktop User-Agent (403 to WebFetch) and read the full table. Every per-bank figure the researcher listed matches the source table exactly, as do the totals 1,426/548 and 1,503/687; 687-548=139 checks out, and August 2024 to January 2026 is 17 months. Added the negative intelligence the researcher omitted: three banks explicitly reject coin machines, which caps that sub-opportunity. One nuance on Moneta: the researcher wrote 'from all 134 branches to 41 of 123' - the 134 is the August-2024 branch count, not a 2025 opening balance, so the two numbers come from different census dates. Comparability caveat: the survey counts what each bank itself calls a branch, and excludes KB's ~200 Modra pyramida 'KB poradenske misto' advisory points and UniCredit's 46 franchise UniCredit Express outlets, all of which are cashless anyway.

verified_signals.entity: Ceska sporitelna - ATM software and hardware incumbency
verified_signals.signal: [STANDING - dated 2023/2024, no current trigger] Ceska sporitelna's recycler fleet is OKI: KAL states CS deployed 250 OKI Cash Recycle ATMs, the 250th announced 15/03/2023, alongside NCR cash recyclers, all running KAL's multivendor Kalignite software. Separately, as of June 2024 CS had migrated 'hundreds of NCR machines' to KAL's Kalignite Hypervisor - Red Hat Linux virtualisation running Windows 10 as a guest operating system - explicitly to decouple the ATM PC-core from the OS, avoid forced PC-core replacement and extend ATM hardware life. CS and KAL announced the world's first production ATM running Windows 10 on a Linux hypervisor in January 2020. KAL states CS has NOT yet extended the Hypervisor to the other ATM brands in its fleet but could do so.
verified_signals.source_name: KAL ATM Software - '250th Cash Recycle ATM' (15/03/2023) and 'Ceska sporitelna boosts ATM lifecycle efficiency with Kalignite Hypervisor' (30/05/2024); world-first announced via Business Wire 15/01/2020
verified_signals.implies: THREAT/qualifier, not an opportunity: CS is a hard multivendor-software incumbency (KAL) on OKI + NCR hardware, and its hypervisor strategy is deliberately designed to DELAY hardware refresh. Negative for pure hardware replacement bids at CS; the only openings are software-agnostic recycler supply, spares and field services.
verified_signals.followup: Establish whether CS has since extended the Hypervisor to the OKI estate, and when the NCR fleet finally ages out - the 2026 fleet is now 1,501 ATMs+payment kiosks and shrinking ~80/year (see the CS H1-2026 signal), which sets the natural replacement rhythm.
verified_signals.verifier_note: kal.com fails TLS verification via WebFetch; retrieved both articles with curl -k plus a desktop User-Agent. The 250 OKI recyclers, the 15/03/2023 date, the co-existing NCR recyclers and the KAL multivendor claim are all stated verbatim. The Hypervisor article (dated 30/05/2024) states verbatim 'As of June 2024, Ceska sporitelna has migrated hundreds of NCR machines to Kalignite Hypervisor', so the researcher's 'hundreds of NCR machines' is correct. CORRECTED the world-first date: the researcher implied the world-first belongs to 30/05/2024, but KAL/CS announced the first production Windows-10-on-Linux-hypervisor ATM in January 2020 (Business Wire, 15/01/2020); 30/05/2024 is only the date of KAL's follow-up case study. Also answered part of the researcher's own followup: KAL says CS has not yet extended the Hypervisor beyond NCR ('If the bank ever wants to extend Kalignite Hypervisor to the other ATM brands in its fleet, it can do so easily'). RE-TAGGED AS STANDING and is_new set to false - the newest evidence here is 2 years old with no deadline, tender or go-live attached. DOWNGRADED opp_size from L to Unscoped: this is competitive-incumbency intelligence with no disclosed procurement event, and nothing in the evidence supports a EUR 1-5m sizing. verified_signals.signal: [STANDING - dated 11/2025] On 20/11/2025 the UOHS concluded that the 'Vklad na kartu' (deposit-to-card) service run by CSOB, Ceska sporitelna and Raiffeisenbank does NOT breach competition or payment rules. The authority expressly distinguished it from the four-bank ATM-sharing project (KB, Moneta, Air Bank, UniCredit): Vklad na kartu involves no network sharing or joint network optimisation, only deposits routed over Mastercard and Visa card rails at any participating bank's deposit ATM.
verified_signals.implies: Enabling condition, not a spend event: the regulatory green light removes the main antitrust blocker to further deposit-ATM interoperability, so additional banks can join either scheme without a competition challenge.
verified_signals.followup: Watch for a fourth bank joining Vklad na kartu - that would be the actual triggering event; the clearance itself carries no budget.
verified_signals.verifier_note: Opened the UOHS release. Confirmed the date (20/11/2025), the three participating banks (CSOB, Ceska sporitelna, Raiffeisenbank), the no-infringement conclusion, and the express distinction from the KB/Moneta/Air Bank/UniCredit network-sharing project on the grounds that Vklad na kartu is card-rails-based and involves no network sharing or optimisation. RE-TAGGED AS STANDING and is_new set to false: 8 months old with no deadline or follow-on trigger. DOWNGRADED opp_size from M to Unscoped - a competition clearance generates no procurement of its own; it only removes a constraint.

verified_signals.entity: Ceska sporitelna / CSOB / Raiffeisenbank - 'Vklad na kartu'
verified_signals.signal: [STANDING - dated 06/2025] Launched 04/06/2025 with a pilot on nearly 40 deposit ATMs and a stated long-term target of more than 1,000 deposit ATMs. The service runs on Mastercard MoneySend and Visa Direct rails (push-payment card rails that credit an account via the card networks rather than the domestic clearing system), credits almost immediately and typically within 30 minutes, and already supports digitalised Mastercard cards in mobile devices and wearables, with Visa support stated as coming. 2024 deposit growth cited at launch: CS +15% by count / +8% by value; CSOB +12.5% / +4.5%; Raiffeisenbank +14% / +6%.
verified_signals.implies: Card-rails deposit switching, ATM application changes at three banks, and dispute/AML monitoring on cross-bank deposits - plus a stated ramp from ~40 to 1,000+ deposit-capable machines.

verified_signals.signal: [STANDING - dated 09/2024, framework now in force] CNB adopted the TIBER-EU framework for threat-led penetration testing (red-team attack simulation against live systems) on 27/09/2024, in preparation for DORA which applied from 17/01/2025. CNB identifies in-scope institutions at least annually ('minimalne jednou rocne') and each must run an advanced test at least once every three years ('alespon jednou za tri roky'), performed during normal operation on systems genuinely used to deliver critical or important functions. CNB published a TIBER-CZ implementation guide (March 2025) and held a second seminar for preselected institutions on 25/03/2025. A separate CNB DORA supervisory questionnaire had a data-collection deadline of 02/03/2026, which has now passed.
verified_signals.source_name: Czech National Bank - 'CNB pristupuje k ramci TIBER-EU', plus CNB TLPT/TIBER framework page and TIBER-CZ implementation guide
verified_signals.implies: Recurring mandatory red-teaming across critical functions - ATM, POS and HSM estates and the managed-service providers that run them fall in scope. A security, HSM and resilient-managed-services selling point, and a compliance hook for incumbent-displacement conversations.
verified_signals.followup: Get CNB's selection criteria and, if obtainable, the TIBER-CZ in-scope list (not public), plus the timing of the next test wave - the first three-year cycle from the 2025 preselection lands in 2027/2028.
verified_signals.verifier_note: Opened the CNB news item and the CNB TLPT/TIBER framework page. Confirmed verbatim: adoption announced 27/09/2024, annual identification of relevant institutions 'minimalne jednou rocne', testing 'alespon jednou za tri roky', tests run 'za provozu, a to na systemech realne vyuzivanych' for critical functions, and the DORA linkage. Added from the CNB framework page: a TIBER-CZ implementation guide published March 2025 and a 25/03/2025 CNB / Czech Banking Association seminar for preselected institutions - both more recent than the researcher's anchor. CORRECTED the deadline field: the researcher carried 02/03/2026 as a live deadline, but that is the CNB DORA supervisory-questionnaire data-collection date and it has already passed as of 31/07/2026, so it is no longer a forward trigger.
